<!-- SHARED DOCUMENT: identical in ohmycoach-mobile, ohmycoach-backend, ohmycoach-web-admin and ohmycoach-marketplace. Do not edit in a single repository. -->

# OhMyCoach Decision Log

> Running record of product and architecture decisions taken during consolidation.
> Convention: conversation with the product owner is in Spanish; **all project documentation is English only**.
> Status values: `DECIDED`, `PROPOSED` (awaiting explicit confirmation), `OPEN`.
> This is the source of truth. `02-business-rules.md`, `03-roles-and-permissions.md` and `04-workout-block-model.md` implement these decisions; if they disagree, fix the document.

## Decided

| ID | Decision | Notes |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| D-001 | **Documentation language is English only.** No Spanish and no Spanglish in documentation, identifiers, enum values, endpoint paths, database objects or file names. | Applies to all three repositories and to the shared documents. Existing Spanish drafts will be replaced, not translated piecemeal, when the consolidated set is generated. |
| D-002 | Payments are **mocked** in the MVP. Stripe, direct debit and real money movement come after user adoption is validated. | The payment flow stays behind a provider interface so Stripe can replace the mock. |
| D-003 | **Mobile app is athlete-facing only** (`NORMAL_USER`, `PRO_ATHLETE`, `OPEN_ATHLETE`): consult programming, log sessions and scores, capture PRs, check in, book specialists, and follow the Marketplace programs the account already has (no browsing, buying, pricing or purchase prompts, D-069). **Web admin is for management.** Staff who log into mobile see the `PRO_ATHLETE` view (they are automatic members of the advanced group, D-046). | Wording widened during reconciliation; the original text said "limited to consulting programming". Amended by D-069. |
| D-004 | Programming is captured **only as structured JSON blocks**. No rich text editor and no text parser. | |
| D-005 | `OPEN_ATHLETE` and the Marketplace are **in the MVP**. Only real charging is post-MVP. | |
| D-006 | A user belongs to **one gym at a time**. Leaving a gym turns the user into `OPEN_ATHLETE`, keeps the account and PR history, and shows the default OhMyCoach theme. | |
| D-007 | **Selling is a capability, not a role.** A user with a *publisher profile* can sell programs. The profile is activated manually by `SUPER_ADMIN`. Sold programs belong to the **person** (`tenant_id` is null), not to a gym. Gym programming (`CLASS`, `ADVANCED`, `CUSTOM`) belongs to the tenant and **cannot be put on sale**. | The web admin shows two contexts for users that have both: "My gym" and "My Marketplace". A program is a first-class entity; every workout belongs to a program. Exact schema is defined in the block/data-model step. |
| D-008 | **A single `COACH` role** replaces `INTERNAL_COACH` and `EXTERNAL_COACH`. Roles are: `NORMAL_USER`, `PRO_ATHLETE`, `OPEN_ATHLETE`, `COACH`, `SPECIALIST`, `OWNER`, `SUPER_ADMIN`. | Coach tools are derived from `tenant_id` (gym tools) and the publisher profile (Marketplace tools). `OWNER` stays separate because it carries tenant administration (staff, white-label) and may also hold a publisher profile. |
| D-009 | `NORMAL_USER` (and every athlete role) can **browse and buy** Marketplace programs, in the Marketplace storefront website (D-069), not in the mobile app. | More contracted programs mean more commission. Amended by D-069. |
| D-010 | Alerts generated from a **Marketplace program** are routed to that program's publisher. | Resolves the "single coach per alert" problem for Marketplace programs only. Gym alert routing: see D-013. |
| D-011 | A gym employee selling on behalf of the gym with revenue sharing is **out of the MVP**. | Content ownership and revenue split are a separate problem. |
| D-012 | `OWNER` accounts and coaches with a publisher profile are **provisioned manually by `SUPER_ADMIN`** in the MVP (sales-led onboarding). Athletes self-register. | |
| D-013 | **Performance-alert recipients are configured per gym program.** (Performance alerts are the rule-based fatigue and movement-block alerts of D-025. Informational messages such as holiday notices are **announcements**, a separate module available for every audience.) Each gym program that produces feedback (`ADVANCED`; `CLASS` has no feedback form, D-023) has a list of recipient coaches, editable only by `OWNER` in the web admin. Default recipients are the program creator and the owner. For a `CUSTOM` plan the recipient is the coach assigned to that plan. If a recipient list is empty, alerts fall back to the owner. | A coach sees only the alerts of programs where they are a recipient. The owner sees all alerts of the tenant but is notified only for programs where the owner is a recipient. Alerts can contain health data, so visibility is need-to-know. |
| D-014 | **Staff notifications are an in-app inbox in the web admin only.** No web push and no email in the MVP. Staff see received alerts when they log in. | Athletes keep mobile push (FCM) for published programming and appointment outcomes. Specialist appointment requests use the same inbox (D-016). |
| D-015 | Each tenant has a `marketplace_visible` switch, **default `true`**, so an owner can hide the Marketplace from their members. | Included by default as recommended; no objection raised. |
| D-016 | **The `SPECIALIST` manages everything in the web admin** with limited access: publish and block availability slots, and accept or reject appointment requests from the internal inbox. No CRM, programming or alerts. | |
| D-017 | A `SPECIALIST` can log into the mobile app and sees the **`PRO_ATHLETE` view** with the gym theme, because access to advanced programming is a staff benefit. | Same rule as `COACH` and `OWNER` on mobile. |
| D-018 | Appointment limit: **one appointment per day per specialist**, and never the same time slot with two different specialists. | Set by default (no preference stated). It resolves the contradiction between the two mobile documents. |
| D-019 | An athlete **can cancel** an appointment until it takes place. A new `CANCELLED` status frees the slot and shows up in the specialist's inbox. No cancellation-window policy in the MVP. | Set by default (no preference stated). |
| D-020 | When a gym has **no active specialist**, the appointments entry is **hidden** from athletes (not locked). When a gym has specialists but none has published availability, the section shows an empty state. The web admin shows the owner a hint to add a specialist. When the owner removes a specialist, **all future appointments of that specialist are cancelled automatically** and the affected athletes are notified. | Closes the specialist topic. |
| D-021 | **Workout session flow for athletes.** In programs that support feedback, each section (block) of the day has a **completion checkbox** the athlete ticks while training. At the end, the athlete gives an **overall status** (`SUCCESS`, `ADJUSTED`, `FAILED`) and an optional comment. If the status is `ADJUSTED` or `FAILED`, the athlete **selects which movements of today's workout were affected** from the list of movements in that day's blocks. | Replaces the three earlier feedback designs. Checkboxes and the form are stored locally and synced through the offline queue. Unchecked blocks are recorded as not completed but do not trigger alerts in the MVP. Warm-up and cool-down text items have no `movement_key` and do not appear in the picker. |
| D-022 | Status enum is `SUCCESS` / `ADJUSTED` / `FAILED`. `SCALED` is not used for feedback because it already names the alternative prescription of a metcon. | Default; no objection raised. |
| D-023 | **Checkboxes and the feedback form exist by program type**: `ADVANCED`, `CUSTOM` and Marketplace programs. Not in `CLASS`. | Default; matches the product owner's description (pro and open athletes). Any athlete who buys a Marketplace program gets it, regardless of level. Score entry for the leaderboard is a separate action (see round 2). |
| D-024 | **Load percentages reference an explicit PR.** A part with percentages carries `percentage_reference`, a key from the PR catalog chosen by the coach in the builder (for example "70% of `POWER_SNATCH`"). The movement performed is independent. No variant-to-PR mapping table. | Default. Resolves the complex RM reference and the `HANG_POWER_SNATCH` versus `POWER_SNATCH` mismatch. Superseded by D-035: the reference lives at **part** level. |
| D-025 | **Alert thresholds (Phase 1, fixed in configuration):** global fatigue = 3 consecutive logged sessions with `ADJUSTED` or `FAILED`; movement block = `ADJUSTED` or `FAILED` on the same movement in 3 consecutive weeks in which it was programmed. Evaluated **per athlete and per program**, so every alert has a single recipient list (D-010, D-013). Phase 2 (rolling baseline) is post-MVP. | Default. Phase 2 needs 6+ months of history and actual weight lifted, which is not captured yet. |
| D-026 | The feedback form opens from a **"Finish workout" button**, not from a specific block. It works for strength-only days and for days with several metcons. The athlete may finish with unchecked blocks. | |
| D-027 | **Leaderboard and scoring.** Only `METCON` blocks can be flagged as scored by the coach, and only with format `FOR_TIME` or `AMRAP`. Days without a scored block have no result capture and no leaderboard. The athlete picks `RX` or `SCALED` with a selector on the METCON; the selector also switches the displayed prescription according to `rx_standard`. If only RX is defined there is no selector and the result is `RX`. **`FOR_TIME`:** the athlete enters the time, which cannot exceed the time cap. If the athlete does not finish, the result is **`CAP + N`**, where `N` is the number of **repetitions remaining** to finish. `CAP + N` applies only when every movement of the scored version is rep-based; if the WOD includes distance or calories (for example a run), a capped athlete is recorded as plain `CAP` with no number. **`AMRAP`:** the athlete enters completed rounds plus the last movement reached and the repetitions done in it, bounded by the prescription; the total is computed. `INTERVALS` WODs (EMOM-style or scored by the sum of times) and Tabata work-rest parts are not scored in the MVP. **Leaderboard:** per day and per program (`CLASS`, `ADVANCED`, and each Marketplace program, see D-060), visible to the program's audience (D-051), with **two sections: `RX` first, then `SCALED`**, each ranked separately. Ranking: `FOR_TIME` ranks finishers by time ascending, then capped athletes by fewest remaining repetitions (plain `CAP` results tie at the end of their section); `AMRAP` ranks by total repetitions. | Score entry exists in `CLASS` too, independently of feedback. Requires structured, fixed repetitions: an `AMRAP` can only be flagged as scored with fixed repetitions per round, and `CAP + N` needs the total repetitions to be computable from `rep_scheme` and `movements[]`; otherwise only the finishing time is captured. Defaults, not explicitly confirmed: each section shows its own Top 10, and `OWNER` and coaches can remove a result from the web admin. |
| D-028 | The user profile has an **`rx_standard`** field (`MEN` or `WOMEN`), chosen at registration and editable, that selects which prescription column is shown. The user's sex is not stored. | Default; no preference stated. |
| D-029 | **Movement catalog is global** and edited only by `SUPER_ADMIN`. Coaches may type a free-text movement when one is missing. Free-text movements do not calculate loads and do not count toward movement-block alerts, but they appear in the feedback picker by name so the coach can read the athlete's report. | Default; no preference stated. |
| D-030 | **Block types (9):** `WARM_UP`, `STRENGTH`, `STRENGTH_COMPLEX`, `INTERVALS`, `ACCESSORY`, `METCON`, `SKILL`, `COOL_DOWN`, `CUSTOM`. `EMOM` is renamed `INTERVALS` (interval length is configurable: 30 s, 60 s, 2:30...). `ACCESSORY` is new: rounds "for quality" of several movements with rests, rep ranges, per-side counts and free loads. `EMOM_ALT` is dropped and `GYMNASTICS` is merged into `SKILL`. A block is one numbered section of the coach's programming and contains one or more **parts** (A, B, C), which replace the flat `items[]`. `METCON` uses `RX` and `SCALED` **versions** (see D-032). | Updated after reviewing six real advanced programs. Final once the six samples validate against the draft schema. Validated against the six real programs. `METCON` formats are `FOR_TIME`, `AMRAP` and `INTERVALS` (`EMOM` removed). |
| D-031 | **Naming of lifts:** `Clean` means Squat Clean and `Snatch` means Squat Snatch. Power variations are always named explicitly. Catalog keys are `SQUAT_CLEAN`, `SQUAT_SNATCH`, `POWER_CLEAN` and `POWER_SNATCH`; the builder resolves the aliases "Clean" and "Snatch" to the squat versions. | Key names are a default; the convention itself comes from the product owner. |
| D-032 | **Structure required in the MVP** (found in six real advanced programs): (1) percentage ranges and RPE as an alternative to percentage; (2) `ramp_up[]`; (3) a `coaching` object on every block (intention, stimulus, form cues, strategy per movement, substitutions, intensity); (4) `parts[]` inside blocks, each with its own videos and optional flag, with one completion checkbox per block; (5) `ACCESSORY` block; (6) `INTERVALS` with configurable interval length, rounds and ranges of intervals with their own intensity; (7) `METCON` versions `RX` and `SCALED`, each with its full definition; (8) structured quantities (load with unit, distance, calories, height or deficit with men/women variants; reps as value, range, per side, maximum or time), where only loads convert between lb and kg; (9) `optional: true` on blocks and parts, excluded from the progress bar. **Text, minor or deferred:** (10) WOD targets as informational `targets`; (11) day metadata: duration in minutes, general intention, closing note; (12) loads derived from a result of the same session (for example 20% of today's 3RM) shown as text; (13) interval WODs scored by the sum of times are displayed but not scored. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-033 | **Programs per gym:** a gym offers `CLASS`, `ADVANCED` and `CUSTOM` plans. There is one `CLASS` program and one `ADVANCED` program per gym, and `CUSTOM` plans are per athlete. An occasional special day such as a "Competitors Track" (a benchmark-style competition stimulus) is a normal workout with an optional day label (`track_label`), not a separate program. | |
| D-034 | **Progress bar accepted (was O-005).** A slim bar pinned under the top app bar shows `completed blocks / checkable blocks` with a label such as "3 of 7 · 43%". At 100% it turns into a "Finish workout" action; the inline button at the end of the list is always available. One bar per workout (day + program), only in programs with checkboxes. Optional blocks and parts are excluded from the count, and parts do not add checkboxes (one per block). Requires a stable `block_id` across edits of a published workout. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-035 | **`percentage_reference` is set at part level** (supersedes the block-level wording of D-024), because parts of one block can use different PRs and a complex can reference another lift (for example 90% of `SQUAT_CLEAN` for Deadlift + Clean Pull). | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-036 | **Media links per movement:** `media_links` are allowed on a part and also on each movement line, so a rounds part with several movements can keep one video per movement. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-037 | Out of the MVP: loads derived from another set of the same session (for example 20% of today's 3RM) stay as text, and interval WODs scored by the sum of times (for example Harvest Moon) are displayed but not scored (confirms items 12 and 13 of D-032). | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-038 | **`pr_family` accepted (was O-006).** Each catalog movement may carry a `pr_family` key naming the PR it is usually measured against. It is defined and edited **only by `SUPER_ADMIN`** in the global catalog (D-029), seeded from the six programs. It is only the builder's default suggestion for `percentage_reference` (D-035): the coach can always override it, and it never changes load calculations. Free-text movements have no `pr_family`, so the coach picks the PR manually. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-039 | **Web admin is a Vite + React SPA** (static build on a CDN). No SSR; Next.js is dropped. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-040 | Catalog key `KB_SUITCASE_HOLD` (Kettlebell Suitcase Hold) is kept; the duplicate `SUITCASE_HOLD` is removed. Seed catalog has 46 movements. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-041 | **Backend runs on ECS Fargate** (one small ARM container for the API, 2 tasks only when availability requires it) with an **EventBridge-scheduled task for the daily alert job**; no Celery and no broker. Tasks run in public subnets behind an Application Load Balancer (no NAT gateway); RDS PostgreSQL is private. Estimated MVP cost with ~100 users: about USD 65 to 95 per month, dominated by fixed costs (ALB, RDS, public IPv4 addresses), not by user count. | Accepted by the product owner. Estimate to be verified in the AWS Pricing Calculator. |
| D-042 | **Access codes.** `BOX_CODE` (gym) and `COACH_CODE` (publisher/coach) stay as two kinds of code but share **one global namespace** and **one input field** in the app; the system resolves which kind it is. Format: lowercase letters, digits and underscore, starting with a letter, 4 to 24 characters, case-insensitive (examples `balerion_ags`, `valhalla_nte`). The owner or coach proposes it and `SUPER_ADMIN` approves it during manual provisioning (D-012). Reserved words are blocked. A code is not self-editable; `SUPER_ADMIN` changes it and the old code is retired permanently. Entering a **gym** code creates a **pending join request** that the owner or a coach approves from the web admin inbox (D-014); a **coach** code is redeemed only in the Marketplace storefront, where it starts a 3-day trial of that coach's program (D-057, D-069); the mobile app has no coach-code entry and treats a coach code as not valid. | Accepted by the product owner. Replaces the 9-digit and `CENT84` formats. Coach-code wording corrected during reconciliation because Marketplace programs are paid subscriptions (D-048). Amended by D-069: the mobile field accepts gym codes only. |
| D-043 | Low-impact defaults accepted: curated set of about 8 bundled typefaces for white-label (`font_family` in tenant config); soft delete (`deleted_at`) with no cascade to athlete logs; published workouts editable with a `revision` counter and stable `block_id` and no version history in the MVP; offline conflicts: server wins for workouts and tenant config, client-generated UUIDs with idempotent writes and last-write-wins for athlete-owned records; web admin access token short-lived in memory plus `httpOnly` refresh cookie (same parent domain), secure storage on mobile; the FastAPI OpenAPI plus the workout JSON Schema are the single contract source; builder uses "+ Add block" buttons with drag-and-drop reordering only; web admin responsive (phone can view, publish and handle inbox, building from scratch on tablet or desktop); staff logs on the `PRO_ATHLETE` view generate no alerts and do not count as active athletes; privacy: privacy notice and explicit consent, account deletion endpoint that removes personal data and anonymizes logs (legal review recommended before launch). | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-044 | **QR check-in.** Each gym has a **printed static QR** (downloaded from the web admin) that contains only the gym code. The athlete scans it with the app; the app sends one minimal request over mobile data (user, gym, time, coordinates). The server accepts it only if the athlete is an **approved member** of that gym, the position is within about **150 m** of the gym location (set once by the owner), and no check-in exists yet that day for that gym. Offline scans are queued with the real scan time and synced later. Check-in records **entry only**; it does not reserve a spot. The owner's web dashboard shows who is **present now** (check-in within the last **60 minutes**), refreshed by polling every 30 to 60 seconds (no WebSockets; resolves H11). Turnstile and electronic door integration is out of the MVP. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-045 | **Weekly streak.** A **session** is one distinct calendar day with either a gym check-in or a completed workout ("Finish workout", D-026). check-in is the way for a gym member who only follows `CLASS` (which has no "Finish workout"), and finishing a workout of any program that has "Finish workout" (`ADVANCED`, `CUSTOM`, any Marketplace program) counts for **every** athlete, including a `NORMAL_USER` subscribed to a Marketplace program and an `OPEN_ATHLETE` (whose only way it is); several events on the same day count once. A week is Monday to Sunday and the weekly goal is **5 sessions** (a global setting, not configurable per gym in the MVP). The streak is the number of consecutive completed weeks that reached the goal; the current week in progress never breaks it. Streak weeks are computed in the user's local time zone. | Accepted by the product owner (goal 5, "Finish workout" for pro and open athletes). Monday start and local time zone are defaults. Week start superseded by D-065 (Sunday to Saturday). |
| D-046 | **Athlete groups and `PRO_ATHLETE`.** Owners and coaches create **groups** of athletes in the web admin CRM (name and members). The gym's `ADVANCED` program is assigned to **one** group, which is its audience. Every approved member of the gym sees `CLASS` by default, with no group needed. `PRO_ATHLETE` is no longer a manual switch: it means "member of the advanced group". An athlete can ask their coach at any time to leave the advanced group and goes back to seeing only `CLASS` (`NORMAL_USER`) while staying in the gym; the coach can add them again. An athlete who leaves the gym (for example to one that is not an OhMyCoach customer) becomes `OPEN_ATHLETE` and keeps account, PRs and history. Groups are also used to filter the CRM and target announcements. Staff (`COACH`, `OWNER`, `SPECIALIST`) are **automatically members of the advanced group** (shown with a staff badge, not removable while they are staff) instead of having a special visibility rule; they are removed from it when they stop being staff. If the athlete joins another customer gym, they are `OPEN_ATHLETE` until the join request is approved, and start there as `NORMAL_USER`. | Accepted by the product owner. Supersedes the manual promotion default. |
| D-047 | **Personal Records (Profile -> Personal Records)**, captured manually by the athlete; 1RM only (no 3RM or 5RM). The old name "Benchmarks" and `BENCHMARK_WODS` are dropped. If a movement of the day uses a percentage and its PR is not captured, the app shows the percentage and a legend inviting the athlete to capture it in Profile -> Personal Records. Sections `STRENGTH` (`BACK_SQUAT`, `DEADLIFT`, `BENCH_PRESS`, `OVERHEAD_STRICT_PRESS`) and `WEIGHTLIFTING` (`FRONT_SQUAT`, `POWER_SNATCH`, `SQUAT_SNATCH`, `SNATCH_BALANCE`, `POWER_CLEAN`, `SQUAT_CLEAN`, `POWER_CLEAN_AND_JERK`, `SPLIT_JERK`, `OVERHEAD_SQUAT`, and similar); `BACK_SQUAT` appears once. Only load PRs can be a `percentage_reference`. Fields: `movement_key`, value, unit, date. Personal Records contain **only** `STRENGTH` and `WEIGHTLIFTING`; the `GYMNASTICS` and `RUNNING` sections are removed from the MVP (those movements stay in the catalog for building workouts). | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-048 | **Mock payments and Marketplace subscriptions.** A Marketplace program is a **monthly subscription aligned to the calendar month**. Buying mid-month charges a prorated amount `price x remaining days / days in month` (purchase day included) and gives access until the end of that month; on day 1 of each month it renews for the full month unless cancelled. Cancelling is allowed at any time, access lasts until month end, and the current month is not refunded. An athlete can hold **several programs at once, including several advanced programs**; each has its own subscription and is cancelled separately, and buying a new program never cancels another. **My Programs** lists the athlete's programs in the mobile app as a read-only list (status and access end date, no prices) and in the storefront, where each subscription can be cancelled separately (D-069). When a subscription expires the content is hidden; logs, scores and PRs are kept. The MVP implements the real cycle (period start and end, status `ACTIVE`, `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED`, proration) behind the payment provider interface (D-002); the mock provider always approves, including renewals, and the storefront shows a clear "test mode, no real charge" label wherever a price or purchase appears (the mobile app shows no prices). Gym membership status (`PAID`, `PENDING`, `OVERDUE`) is set manually by the owner in the CRM as a record only; it does not block access or demote the athlete. The `SUPER_ADMIN` revenue monitor (H13) and the ~20% commission are postponed. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-049 | **Post-MVP payment direction.** The gym membership (real-world service) can be paid in the mobile app and charged recurrently (card on file / direct debit) through the payment provider (Stripe), because real-world services do not fall under the app stores' in-app purchase rules. Card data is handled only by the payment provider's hosted fields; neither OhMyCoach servers nor gym owners and coaches ever see or store card numbers. Owners set plans and prices and see only payment status in the web admin. Paid Marketplace programs (digital content) are sold only through web checkout in the Marketplace storefront (D-069), never through in-app purchase. | Direction accepted by the product owner; no change to the MVP. Channel decision closed by D-069. |
| D-050 | **One printed QR per gym** for joining and checking in. A member who scans it checks in; a non-member who scans it sends a pending join request (D-042). | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-051 | **Leaderboard audience:** each program's leaderboard is visible to that program's audience (`CLASS`: all approved members; `ADVANCED`: advanced group, which includes staff). Staff results appear with a staff badge and can be removed by the owner or coaches (D-027). | Accepted by the product owner; staff badge is a default. |
| D-052 | **Mobile targets Android and iOS from day one** (single Flutter codebase); the first store publication is Android. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-053 | **User-facing copy lives in i18n locale files.** Documentation cites the key and the English source string; Spanish copy lives in the Spanish locale file. | Accepted by the product owner (was O-003). |
| D-054 | **Streak foundation for future periods.** The MVP shows only weekly streaks (D-045), but the model must allow a monthly streak and milestone messages (for example "You have trained a full month in a row at <gym>. Congratulations!") without a data migration: store one record per athlete per session day with its source (check-in or finished workout), derive streaks from those records with a period type (`WEEK` now, `MONTH` later) and a goal, and keep a generic achievements/milestones concept. The definition of a completed month is decided when the feature is built. | Requirement accepted by the product owner. |
| D-055 | **No free Marketplace programs.** A program must have a price above a platform minimum; a publisher cannot give programs away. The only free access is the platform-controlled trial of a coach code (see Q-007 once confirmed). | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-056 | **Announcements.** Owners and coaches publish informational announcements (for example a holiday schedule) to all members or to a group. Each announcement has an optional **"notify athletes"** push (FCM), off by default to avoid spam. Athletes can react with emojis. Announcements are separate from performance alerts (D-013). | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-057 | **Coach code = 3-day trial.** Redeeming the code of a coach with a publisher profile **in the Marketplace storefront** starts a **3-day free trial** of one of that coach's Marketplace programs, once per athlete per program. When the trial ends the program is hidden in the mobile app, which shows no prompt to subscribe (D-069); the storefront shows the option to subscribe (D-048). Only Marketplace programs can be trialled (gym programs are not sold); the trial is reachable only through the code, not from the storefront shelf; the publisher can switch the trial off per program. | Accepted by the product owner. |
| D-058 | **`CUSTOM` plans.** A coach creates a `CUSTOM` program for one athlete from that athlete's CRM profile and assigns it; payment between athlete and gym happens outside the app in the MVP. A gym member without one sees a **locked card** with the legend *"Get in touch with your coach to find out how we can help you reach your goals"* and a button that sends an **in-app personalized plan request** to the gym inbox (owner and coaches, D-014). One open request per athlete at a time; any recipient can mark it handled. `OPEN_ATHLETE` does not see the card. | Accepted by the product owner (option B). Request lifecycle details are defaults. |
| D-059 | **Owners and coaches can sell in the Marketplace** once `SUPER_ADMIN` activates their publisher profile (D-007, D-008, D-012), which is how the platform earns a commission (post-MVP, D-048). What is sold is always a separate Marketplace program owned by the person; a gym's own `CLASS`, `ADVANCED` and `CUSTOM` programs cannot be sold. Duplicating a day from a gym program into a Marketplace program is allowed as an editing convenience, and the two programs stay independent. | Accepted by the product owner; the duplication convenience is a default. |
| D-060 | **Marketplace leaderboards and streaks.** An athlete subscribed to a Marketplace program (for example a `NORMAL_USER` of gym A who subscribes to a program published by gym B) takes part in **that program's leaderboard** among its subscribers, with the same scoring rules as D-027, and finishing its workouts counts for the weekly streak (D-045). Leaderboards show the athlete's display name only, and athletes can hide themselves from leaderboards in their profile settings. | Accepted by the product owner; the display name and hide option are defaults. |
| D-061 | **Default theme and bundled typefaces.** The default "Fitness Dark Theme" palette and the curated set of 8 bundled typefaces are fixed in `theme/theme-tokens.json`. Palette: background `#0E0F12`, surface `#181A1F`, primary `#FF5A1F` (text on it `#0E0F12`), accent `#2DD4BF`, text `#F2F3F5`, secondary text `#A3A8B3`, success `#34D399`, adjusted `#F5B83D`, error `#FF6B6B`; all pass WCAG AA on the background. Typefaces (open licenses, bundled in the apps, no runtime download): `inter` (default), `roboto`, `montserrat`, `poppins`, `oswald`, `barlow`, `rubik`, `bebas_neue`. `font_family` in the tenant configuration holds one of these keys; the backend rejects any other value, the web admin selector lists them and the mobile app bundles them. | Accepted by the product owner. Completes D-043. Applications may use the system font until the font files are bundled. |
| D-062 | **Product language is Spanish only.** Every user-facing surface (mobile app, web admin, and any email or push message the backend sends) is shown in Spanish (`es`). There is no language selector and the device or browser language is ignored. English stays the language of code and documentation (D-001); the `en` locale files remain the source strings that documentation cites (D-053) and the fallback for missing keys, and are not offered to users. The backend keeps the `locale` field (`en` or `es`) in the contract for a future multi-language release; clients always send `es`. All Spanish copy uses the informal **"tú"** register (for example "Inicia sesión", "Tu contraseña") in the mobile app, the web admin, emails and push messages. | Accepted by the product owner. Closes web admin WQ-002. "Tú" register added 2026-11-11. Supersedes "follows the device locale" in mobile `docs/04`. English as a user option is post-MVP. |
| D-063 | **Status colors and status tones.** (1) The D-061 status colors are tuned for the dark default theme and fail WCAG AA on light backgrounds, so `theme/theme-tokens.json` adds `status_on_light`: success `#1B7E5A`, adjusted `#966708`, error `#CC3333` (the D-061 hues, darkened; each is at least 4.5:1 on `#FFFFFF` and `#F5F5F5`, and white text on them is at least 4.5:1). The web admin light theme uses `status_on_light`. In the mobile app, a tenant theme whose background contrasts more with `#0E0F12` than with `#FFFFFF` is treated as light and uses `status_on_light`; otherwise it uses the D-061 values. Gyms cannot customize status colors. (2) Every status is shown with one of four tones: **success** (done or positive), **adjusted** (waiting or needs attention), **error** (negative or overdue) and **neutral** (closed, inactive or not important; the theme's secondary text color, no extra token). Status is never conveyed by color alone: it always carries a label or an icon. (3) Mapping: gym membership payment `PAID` success, `PENDING` neutral, `OVERDUE` error; join request `APPROVED` success, `PENDING` adjusted, `REJECTED` error, `CANCELLED` neutral; session result `SUCCESS` success, `ADJUSTED` adjusted, `FAILED` error; Marketplace subscription `ACTIVE` success, `CANCELLED` adjusted (access continues until month end), `EXPIRED` neutral; specialist appointment `ACCEPTED` success, `REQUESTED` adjusted, `REJECTED` error, `CANCELLED` neutral; workout `PUBLISHED` success, `DRAFT` neutral. The staff inbox status (`NEW`, `READ`, `RESOLVED`) is shown with emphasis, not a status tone. A new status enum follows the same four-tone rule without a new decision. | Accepted by the product owner. Completes D-061. Closes web admin WQ-004 and the status-color part of mobile Q-M009 (the tenant color format stays open). |
| D-064 | **What athletes see and how far ahead coaches program.** Athletes see the published workouts of the **current calendar week only**: Sunday to Saturday in the athlete's time zone (the same week as the mobile and web calendars). Published workouts of future weeks stay hidden until their week starts; the backend enforces it (the feed never returns a date after the Saturday of the caller's current week). Past weeks stay visible read-only, within the athlete's access to the program (D-048 still hides expired Marketplace content), with the athlete's own logs and scores; they are fetched online on demand and are not cached on the device. The device caches only the current week plus athlete records pending sync. Drafts are never visible to athletes. Coaches and publishers can program and publish **any number of weeks ahead**; there is no horizon limit. A published workout cannot be unpublished in the MVP; mistakes are fixed by editing it or deleting it (soft delete, D-043). | Accepted by the product owner. Scheduled publishing is post-MVP. |
| D-065 | **Streak week Sunday to Saturday.** The streak week runs **Sunday to Saturday** in the athlete's time zone (supersedes "Monday to Sunday" in D-045), so the app has a single week definition (D-064). The goal stays **5 sessions** per week. Saturday and Sunday are usually rest days and are not required, but a session on either day counts and can make up for a missed weekday. The rest of D-045 stands. | Accepted by the product owner; to be revisited with pilot feedback. |
| D-066 | **Programming notifications without spam.** (1) The web admin offers **Publish week**: it publishes every draft of one program's calendar week in one action and, when "notify athletes" is on, sends **one** push. (2) Publishing a single day keeps its own "notify athletes" switch. (3) The backend sends **at most one programming push per program, per athlete, per local day**; extra requests are dropped silently. (4) No push is sent for a workout outside the athlete's current week (D-064): the switch is disabled for future weeks. (5) Saving changes to a published workout never notifies. Push is implemented in backend M5; the contract and the builder support it from M2 and W4. | Accepted by the product owner. A deferred push when a future week becomes visible is post-MVP. |
| D-067 | **Assigned coach of a `CUSTOM` plan.** A `CUSTOM` program has an `assigned_coach_id`: by default the coach who creates the plan; the `OWNER` or the current assigned coach can change it, and it must be an active `COACH` or `OWNER` of the same gym. The assigned coach receives the plan's alerts (D-013). If that user stops being staff, the plan's alerts fall back to the owner until another coach is assigned. The field exists from backend M2 (when `CUSTOM` programs can be created) so M5 needs no migration. | Accepted by the product owner. Closes backend Q-041. Choosing another coach is not a caller-supplied `coach_id` (D-043): the backend validates the target against the caller's tenant. |
| D-068 | **Spanish workout vocabulary.** Labels generated from the workout model use the glossary in `04-workout-block-model.md` section 11, identical in the mobile app and the web admin. CrossFit jargon stays in English (For Time, AMRAP, RX, Scaled, Tabata, Metcon, Time cap, Skill, Cool down); everything else is translated (for example Calentamiento, Fuerza, Accesorios, Aproximaciones, Descanso, rondas, por lado). `EMOM` is not used as a label; the interval clock is shown instead. Coach-written text is shown as written. Numbers use the `es-MX` locale (decimal point); ranges use an en dash with spaces and the unit once (`RPE 8.5 – 9`, `78 – 83%`); `reps_by_round` keeps `9-7-5` (section 11, "Numbers and ranges"). | Accepted by the product owner: the mixed vocabulary is how the target athletes speak. Number and range format added 2026-11-11 (mobile Q-M014). |
| D-069 | **Marketplace lives in its own website, outside the mobile app and the web admin.** A fifth repository, `ohmycoach-marketplace` (the "storefront"), is a public website where athletes and publishers sign in with their OhMyCoach account. It owns: the public catalog and program pages, athlete registration and login, checkout (mocked, D-002), subscription management and cancellation (D-048), redeeming coach codes for the 3-day trial (D-057), and the publisher panel (create the program record, description, price, listing and trial switch, subscribers). **Mobile app rule:** it contains no Marketplace shelf, no purchase or cancel flow, no prices, no coach-code entry, and no text, button or link that invites users to buy or points to an external purchase (for any store storefront). It only consumes what the account already has: programs appear in Home, with checkboxes, feedback, scores and leaderboards (D-060), and My Programs is a read-only list. A coach code typed in the app is reported as not valid. When access ends the program silently disappears. Empty states never mention buying or a website. **Web admin rule:** no catalog, pricing, subscriber list or "My Marketplace" context. A publisher still builds and publishes the workouts of a `MARKETPLACE` program in the web admin builder and receives its performance alerts there. Athlete roles may sign into the storefront; the web admin still rejects them; `SUPER_ADMIN` provisioning of publishers (D-012) is unchanged. `marketplace_visible` (D-015) now hides the catalog from members of that tenant in the storefront. The storefront follows D-062: Spanish only, informal "tú", no language selector. The storefront keeps its own session: the same account, but a refresh cookie separate from the web admin's (D-043), so signing in or out in one website never affects the other in the same browser (contract: `client: STOREFRONT`, backend Q-045). | Accepted by the product owner. Motive: avoid app-store policy risk and store commissions on digital content, and because the calendar-month proration of D-048 does not fit store subscription mechanics. Gym membership payment in the app (real-world service, D-049) is unaffected. Residual risk: store review may still question content bought on the web and consumed in the app; mitigate with review notes and a demo account (Apple guideline 3.1.3(b) allows it only when the same items are also sold in the app, so approval is not guaranteed). |
| D-070 | **Tenant theme colors.** The tenant colors (primary, accent, background, text) are `#RRGGBB` hex strings without alpha. The backend accepts upper or lower case, stores them in upper case, and rejects anything else with 422 `REQUEST_VALIDATION_FAILED` (path to the field); it validates the format only, never the contrast. The web admin white-label wizard checks every color pair the app uses (text on background, text on surface, text on primary, primary on background) against WCAG AA and **warns** with the failing pairs and a live preview, but **lets the owner save** so a gym can keep its brand colors. The mobile app compensates: it picks the text color on primary by contrast, uses `status_on_light` on light backgrounds (D-063), and falls back to the D-061 value for any stored color it cannot parse. | Accepted by the product owner. Closes backend Q-027, mobile Q-M009 (format part) and web WQ-005. |
| D-071 | **Rest lines inside a sequence.** The movement lists of `WOD` versions, `ROUNDS` parts and `INTERVALS` groups accept a **rest line** `{ "rest": Rest }` (fixed seconds, a range or `as_needed`) between movement lines. A rest line splits the sequence into for-time stretches and repeats with `rounds`; a rest after the last movement of the last round is not performed. This covers "each round for time, rest between rounds" (for example 6 rounds with 2:00 rest) and rests in the middle of a round (for example "Row, Run, Rest 1:00, Run, Row"). A scored `FOR_TIME` with rest lines scores the **total clock time, rests included**, and its time cap is measured on the same clock; rest lines never count as repetitions (AMRAP totals, `CAP + N`). The timer shows each rest line as a countdown. Example `competition.json`. Out of the MVP and kept as notes: work:rest ratios ("Rest 1:1"), a time cap per round, several scaled options, scores of strength tests, max distance or "Death By" (published unscored), unit conversion of distances (shown as prescribed), and two sessions on the same day for one program (the coach publishes one session, or adds the second as optional blocks). | Accepted by the product owner after reviewing nine competition-program days. Schema change: `RestLine` and `SequenceItem` in `workout.schema.json`. |

## Reconciliation notes (old business rules versus decisions)
Items of the legacy (pre-consolidation) business-rules document that this log supersedes. The consolidated documents follow the decisions, not the old text.
- Rule 1 roles table (7 roles with `INTERNAL_COACH`/`EXTERNAL_COACH`): replaced by D-008; `SPECIALIST` surface closed by D-016/D-017.
- Rule 3 (Benchmarks, four categories, gymnastics checkbox, running): replaced by D-047. PR history stays append-only (each update is a new record, latest is current) so passive progress charts still work.
- Rule 4: `ADVANCED` is **no longer openly visible** to the community; it is visible only to the advanced group and to staff (D-046). `CUSTOM` assignment and the contact button: see Q-001.
- Rule 5 (2-step form, "3 to 4 sessions"): replaced by D-021 to D-026.
- Rule 7: streak "1 week or 1 month" replaced by D-045 (weekly only, goal 5; monthly streak is out of the MVP). Leaderboard "daily Top 10 across all classes" replaced by D-027 (per program, RX then SCALED).
- Rule 8: mechanism, validity window and offline behavior defined by D-044. One QR for joining and checking in: D-050.
- Rule 9: a new `BOX_CODE` creates a pending join request (D-042). The questions "what happens to level, logs and alerts" and "does membership expiry demote the account" are closed by D-046 and D-048.
- Rule 11: closed by D-048.
- Rule 2: single app with a per-tenant dynamic theme is confirmed by the product description and all decisions; typography is `font_family` (D-043).

## Open questions
None at the time of consolidation (D-001 to D-071 are closed).
